title: POC acceptance observability & gating signoff
summary: Redwood and Nimbus align on go/no-go thresholds for the POC: latency and stability SLOs, quality gates (accuracy/hallucination thresholds), cost targets, and an agreed reporting format. Agreed benchmark runbook, dataset slices, and timeline: 2-week bench run + 1-week analysis and signoff. Action items assigned for benchmark scripts, RBAC+security checklist, and scheduling a live run in Nimbus staging VPC.
next_steps: Redwood to share benchmark runner script and test dataset links by 2025-11-21
Nimbus to provision staging cluster with sample traffic and provide access by 2025-11-24
Schedule live benchmark run window (2 days) for week of 2025-12-01

Owner: Tom Reeves (Nimbus) - Confirm VPC peering and KMS access for test environment; send network diagram. Due: 2025-11-24

Owner: Jules Kim (Redwood) - Run initial smoke test and share logs with Priya. Due: 2025-11-26
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-19
Start time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Jules (Redwood SE), Maya (Nimbus HoML), Rajan (Nimbus Platform), Clara (PM), Tom (Security), Priya (Data Sci)
---
[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, we have Maya, Rajan, Clara, Tom, Priya on Nimbus side, and Samir and Jules with me from Redwood. Um, the goal today is to lock the acceptance gates for the POC and the reporting format so the bench run can be run next week.
[00:23] Maya (Nimbus): Yep, that's right. We want clarity on pass/fail so stakeholders can sign off. Primary things for us: latency p95, inference cost per 1M tokens, and a hallucination / factuality threshold for our doc extract workload.
[00:41] Samir (Redwood): Makes sense. We'll propose concrete numbers and the runbook. At a high level we usually validate: stability (no crashes for N hours), latency SLOs, throughput targets, and quality — which for you translates to extract precision and false positive rate.
[01:05] Rajan (Nimbus): For sizing, our staging mimics peak bursts: ~400 concurrent requests with average 120 tokens output per request. Average QPS during peak ~55. We'll provide historical distribution.
[01:28] Jules (Redwood): Thanks. For the bench we'll ask you to provide a representative 10k query slice and a smaller 500-query diagnostic set for latency profiling. The acceptance tests will run both.
[01:50] Clara (Nimbus): Quick question: do you run the bench from Redwood-hosted infra or inside our VPC? Security would prefer inside our VPC to mirror network effects.
[02:03] Tom (Nimbus - Security): Yes, we need the run to be within our staging V P C and have KMS keys available; we also need audit logs turned on.
[02:16] Alex (Redwood): That's fine — we support Private POC runs in-customer VPC. We'll need a short checklist to configure IAM/KMS and the peering. I'll send the network checklist.
[02:29] Maya: Cool. On thresholds: we propose go/no-go as: latency p95 <= 300ms for single-token streaming case, p95 <= 800ms for full 120-token outputs? I want to know what Redwood's typical numbers look like.
[02:51] Samir: I'll be frank — the numbers depend on model size and quantization. For a 7B quantized variant we can typically hit p95 ~220-350ms for 120-token outputs on our optimized runtime if KV caching is working well; for 70B that shifts a lot. Do you have a model family pinned?
[03:15] Priya (Nimbus): We're planning to test both an open 13B and a tuned 7B quantized variant. The 13B is our baseline for quality; 7B is the cost-optimized candidate.
[03:33] Alex: Perfect. So acceptance gates we recommend:
- Stability: no server errors >0.5% over a 1-hour run
- Latency: p95 per-request for your workload: 13B baseline target p95 <= 700ms; 7B candidate p95 <= 350ms
- Throughput: system sustains the peak burst profile (55 QPS with 400 concurrency) with less than 10% degraded tail ops
- Quality: F1 on entity extraction >= 0.86 for baseline, and >=0.80 for candidate; hallucination rate <= 4% (measured on the 10k slice)
[04:07] Maya: That looks reasonable. The hallucination metric — we need a definition. Is that extraneous facts flagged by human labelers?
[04:18] Jules: We define hallucination as any generated fact not present in the source doc or contradicted by it. We'll provide annotation guidelines and a sample labeling spreadsheet. The benchmark will compute hallucination rate as hallucinated spans / total predicted spans.
[04:40] Rajan: On cost — what's the expected per-1M-token cost for the two candidates? We need to compare to our current infra.
[04:49] Samir: For hosted Redwood numbers, rough ballpark: 7B quantized candidate ~ $25-40 per 1M output tokens depending on batching; 13B ~ $80-120 per 1M. In your private run costs will be mostly infra; we'll estimate GPU-hours required and translate into cost equivalents in the report.
[05:12] Tom: Security ask: audit logs, RBAC, and proof of SOC2 type II — we need to see the docs.
[05:19] Alex: We'll attach our SOC2 and ISO docs in the follow-up. For the POC run inside your VPC we'll enable enhanced audit logging and provide temporary service accounts with least privilege.
[05:33] Maya: About reporting format: we prefer a CSV with per-query rows: query_id, model, latency_p50/p95, tokens_out, tokens_in, error_flag, predicted_entities, hallucination_flag, cost_estimate, plus a summary PDF with plots. Is that doable?
[05:52] Jules: Yes — our standard acceptance CSV matches that. We'll also provide a Grafana dashboard snapshot for SLA traces. The CSV must include raw scoring columns so you can reproduce metrics.
[06:09] Priya: Also include raw model logits or confidence isn't possible for some models, right?
[06:16] Samir: We can include token-level log-probs if model and privacy allow; for tuned close-source variants that might not be available. We'll include what we can and note gaps.
[06:29] Clara: Timeline check: we want the bench run and a signoff within two weeks. Is that realistic?
[06:35] Alex: Proposed timeline:
- By 11/21 Redwood delivers bench runner and acceptance template
- By 11/24 Nimbus provides dataset and staging infra
- 11/25-11/28 run window (we suggest two-day window within these dates)
- 11/29-12/01 analysis and results pack, signoff call on 12/02
That's effectively a 2-week cadence from today.
[07:01] Maya: Tight but okay. We have an internal decision meeting on 12/05 so signoff before then is important.
[07:08] Rajan: A small nit: we need the bench to simulate prefix caching misses sometimes — our real traffic has a heavy long-tail of new prompts. Can your runner vary cache hit ratio?
[07:20] Jules: Yes — the runner has config knobs: cache_hit_ratio, batch sizes, and concurrent open streams. We'll set a scenario with 30% cache hits and 70% cold starts to match your traffic profile.
[07:35] Tom: Regarding data residency — some docs are EU-only. For those we'll mask personally identifiable fields. We'll provide redaction rules.
[07:45] Alex: We'll account for redaction and note any quality delta. If masking alters quality significantly we'll annotate that in the report.
[07:55] Priya: For acceptance analysis, can you include bootstrapping for confidence intervals around the hallucination metric? We want statistical rigor.
[08:02] Samir: Absolutely — we'll compute 95% CIs and include p-values for candidate vs baseline differences.
[08:12] Maya: Another question on fallbacks: if the candidate fails latency but passes quality, we might accept with a degraded SLA if cost savings are above X. Can we encode conditional acceptance?
[08:27] Alex: We can add a weighted rubric: default is hard gates, but you can elect for conditional acceptance: e.g., if latency p95 within 1.5x target but cost savings >30% and quality delta <=2 points, then recommend acceptance for a phased rollout. We'll add that as an appendix to the acceptance doc.
[08:51] Clara: Good. For the acceptance document, include a per-metric pass/fail column and an overall recommendation (Pass / Conditional Pass / Fail) with rationale.
[08:59] Jules: Noted. We'll implement that template.
[09:05] Rajan: On instrumentation — we need request IDs propagated so we can match logs to CSV rows.
[09:12] Samir: Runner will include an example header injection and request_id propagation; we just need your side to accept and echo request_id in logs.
[09:23] Maya: Ok, final checklist: thresholds restated?
[09:27] Alex: Restating:
- Stability: error_rate < 0.5% over 1-hour steady run
- Latency p95: 13B <= 700ms, 7B <= 350ms
- Throughput: sustain 55 QPS with under 10% degraded tail ops
- Quality: extraction F1 >= 0.86 baseline, >= 0.80 candidate; hallucination rate <= 4%
- Cost: per-1M token targets to be estimated; acceptance can use conditional rubric if cost delta used for phased acceptance
[09:54] Priya: That matches our internal expectations. We'll run a small manual audit on a random 500 samples to sanity check labeling.
[10:01] Alex: Great. Anything else on run mechanics?
[10:05] Tom: Please include contact for infra escalation during the run — network, infra, Redwood SE.
[10:11] Alex: I'll include a runbook with on-call contacts and normal/urgent escalation paths.
[10:18] Maya: Ok let's summarize next steps and owners.
---
Recap (verbatim):
- Samir (Redwood) to push benchmark runner + README (due 11/21)

[11:12] Alex: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the repo link and calendar invite for the run window.
[11:18] Maya: Thanks — appreciate the clarity. Looking forward to seeing the runner.
[11:22] Alex: Okay, meeting adjourned.
